author: Associated Press
description:
US President Donald Trump on Sunday played down the need for his administration to check the development of artificial intelligence, saying he worried about ceding America’s edge over China in a global competition and that winning would help address the risks from the advancing technology.
While acknowledging the need for some regulation, Trump provided no specifics about potential rules and attributed warnings about the technology moving too quickly and with little oversight to “negative...
title: Trump downplays need to check AI development, says he is unwilling to cede edge to China

author: Seong Hyeon Choi
description:
Last month, the People’s Liberation Army released footage showing its H-6N bomber flying with a nuclear-capable Jing Lei-1 (JL-1) air-launched ballistic missile (ALBM), offering a rare look at China’s airborne nuclear strike capability.
The H-6N is one of the latest modernised variants of the H-6, the country’s only strategic bomber. Its flight carrying the ALBM during a joint anti-ship exercise was featured in a documentary by state broadcaster CCTV for the PLA’s 99th anniversary.
The unveiling...
title: For China, H-6N bomber enhances nuclear deterrence and second-strike capability

author: Fan Chen
description:
A leading South China Sea analyst has urged Chinese think tanks to recruit AI talent for the “public opinion war” over the disputed waters.
Wu Shicun, the founding president of China’s National Institute for South China Sea Studies, said Chinese humanities and social science research had traditionally operated in a “lone-wolf” fashion and lacked interdisciplinary diversity.
“The situation in the South China Sea is likely to evolve into a complex, multilayered competition … Cognitive and public...
title: Does Beijing need AI talent in ‘public opinion war’ over South China Sea?

author: Ling Xin
description:
China’s FAST telescope has compiled the world’s largest catalogue of neutral hydrogen beyond the Milky Way, replacing a long-dominant US survey as the main reference for mapping the gas that fuels the formation of stars and galaxies.
The FAST All-Sky H I Survey (FASHI), conducted with the 500-metre (1,640-foot) radio dish in southwest China’s Guizhou province, released its second batch of data this week. It contains 156,411 extragalactic sources – nearly five times the number detected by the...
title: China’s FAST telescope maps neutral hydrogen, the cosmic gas for making stars

author: Alyssa Chen
description:
Japanese fashion brand WEGO has scrapped a plan to launch a new range in collaboration with the hit anime and manga franchise My Hero Academia after it triggered an angry backlash from Chinese consumers.
The Tokyo-based company triggered an outcry on Chinese social media after announcing it would release an exclusive range of My Hero Academia-themed clothing.
The franchise was widely condemned in China over a 2020 controversy about a character that conducted lethal human experiments – a topic...
title: Japan’s WEGO fashion brand is latest firm to feel force of Chinese consumer backlash

author: Zhang Tong
description:
Chinese scientists say they have devised a new technique for refining oil that cuts the amount of energy consumed during the process by roughly 90 per cent.
If the technology used in the study could be scaled up for industry, it would not only greatly reduce production costs and emissions, but also make the process more precise and boost product value.
Crude oil cannot be turned directly into petrol or plastics.
Instead, refineries must separate it into different parts before each one can be put...
title: Chinese scientists develop new oil refining method that may cut energy use by 90%

author: Dannie Peng
description:
Chinese scientists say they have discovered a massive underwater mineral deposit in the western Pacific that is remarkably rich in gold and silver.
According to a report by state broadcaster CCTV on Friday, the discovery was made during a joint scientific expedition involving several Chinese academic institutions.
The ores within this seabed hydrothermal field – an area where hot, mineral-rich water shoots out from openings on the ocean floor – are exceptionally rich in precious metals. Silver,...
title: Chinese scientists find ‘extremely high-value’ underwater gold mine in Pacific

author: Cao Jiaxuan,Khushboo Razdan
description:
Chinese President Xi Jinping pledged on Sunday to help Brics countries develop and apply open-source large language models and build smart manufacturing factories.
Speaking at the second day of the Brics summit in New Delhi, he identified these as two out of five key initiatives to promote economic growth and technological development in the Global South.
Xi also said Beijing would offer to train young talent from other member states in advanced technology and innovation, according to state news...
title: Chinese leader pledges to help Brics nations with AI and smart manufacturing

author: Jevans Nyabiage
description:
China is moving early to secure a role in Sudan’s reconstruction, pursuing port and power agreements with the army-backed government while the war continues and many Western countries maintain only a limited presence.
One expert also said Beijing was using the prospect of future investment as a bilateral incentive to encourage warring parties to cease hostilities.
Sudan signed an agreement with the China Harbour Engineering Company in July to upgrade existing ports and build new ones. Meanwhile,...
title: China bets on early port and power deals in Sudan to secure post-war economic edge

author: SCMP
description:
This article was first published on September 10, 1976.
Sense of grief in Hongkong
A deep sense of grief was felt by great numbers of the people in Hongkong yesterday (September 9, 1976) when radio and television stations flashed the news of the Chairman’s passing. The news brought a cloud of gloom over celebrations of the mid-autumn festivities. Flags at a number of major building and hotels, – including the Bank of China – were flown at half-mast within an hour of the announcement.
Hongkong...
title: Hong Kong mourns Mao Zedong’s death in 1976 –  SCMP archive

author: Dannie Peng
description:
Denisovan remains discovered in southwestern China reveal that Yunnan province’s warm, biodiverse plateau was a “hunting paradise” for the hominins during a global glacial period, according to new research published in the journal Nature.
Within the region’s coniferous forests and forest-steppe environments, this archaic human group established a stable subsistence pattern highly adapted to local resources through specialised hunting and the intensive exploitation of animals.
The extinct...
title: Denisovan fossils in China reveal an ancient ‘hunting paradise’

author: Deepa Padmanaban
description:
Some of my earliest memories of Bengaluru, where I spent my summer holidays, are of looking up in wonder at the towering canopy of trees in Cubbon Park. Even in the height of summer, Bengaluru could be cool enough to require a light jacket. Today, the iconic Cubbon Park, the pride of the city I now call home, is under threat. So is Lalbagh Botanical Garden, another of the city’s iconic green spaces, with roots stretching back more than 250 years.
On a Sunday morning in Bengaluru last month,...
title: Warming cities can’t afford to sacrifice their urban parks

author: Xinlu Liang
description:
China’s new draft law on combating cross-border corruption is as much a weapon against foreign interference as it is a tool against illicit financial flows, analysts say.
The draft sets out ways to block extraterritorial investigations and to retaliate against foreign anti-corruption enforcement, drawing a firm legal boundary against foreign jurisdictions while establishing its own mechanism to police overseas assets.
In doing so, legal specialists warn, Beijing is also creating a double-edged...
title: China’s anti-corruption law is going global. What does it mean for overseas firms?
